title: The Age of Optimal Decisions
subtitle: What prescriptive analytics is, and your first linear program — a bakery deciding how much bread and cake to make

objectives.title: Locate Prescriptive on the Analytics Map
objectives.description: Descriptive tells you what happened. Predictive tells you what will happen. Prescriptive tells you what to DO — and that is where the money is.

objectives.title: Formulate a Complete Linear Program
objectives.description: Decision variables, objective, constraints. The bakery problem: maximize 50B + 60C subject to demand, oven time, and labor.

objectives.title: Solve It Graphically
objectives.description: Draw the constraints, shade the feasible set, slide the iso-profit line — and discover why the optimum always lives at a corner.

objectives.title: Solve It with an Industrial Solver
objectives.description: The same model in gurobipy: eleven lines of Python that find the provably best production plan in milliseconds.

agenda.title: Welcome & The Course Ahead
agenda.description: Introductions, what prescriptive analytics is, and the semester arc: linear, network, integer, and nonlinear optimization, then Markov chains, deep learning, and reinforcement learning.
bulletPoints: Data doesn't make money — decisions do
Every session: a business problem → a model → hands-on Python

agenda.title: The Bakery Problem
agenda.description: A bakery makes bread ($50/batch) and cake ($60/batch), can sell at most 90 and 60 batches a week, and is limited by 4,650 minutes of oven time and 4,200 minutes of labor. What should it produce?
bulletPoints: Translating the story into the three-ingredient grammar: variables, objective, constraints

agenda.title: Solving It by Picture: The Feasible Set
agenda.description: Each constraint is a line; together they carve out the green feasible region. Every point inside is a legal production plan — but which one is best?
bulletPoints: Intercepts tell the story: labor alone allows 140 breads or 70 cakes; the oven allows 77.5 breads or 103.3 cakes
Four constraints, one polygon of possibility

agenda.title: Break
agenda.description: Stretch, coffee, meet a future teammate.

agenda.title: Iso-Profit Lines & the Corner-Point Principle
agenda.description: Can we make $1,500? $3,000? $6,000? Sliding the profit line outward until it last touches the feasible set reveals the optimum: 40 breads + 50 cakes = $5,000 — at a corner, where oven and labor are both fully used.
bulletPoints: $6,000 is impossible — the line leaves the feasible region entirely
The optimum of a linear program always sits at a corner of the feasible set

agenda.title: What-If Analysis: A Preview of Sensitivity
agenda.description: The world changes — does the decision? Bread profit drops to $40: same plan, less profit. Drops to $20: the optimum jumps to a different corner (20 breads, 60 cakes). At exactly $30, two corners tie. And 75 extra oven minutes buys $40 of profit.
bulletPoints: Decisions are stable within ranges, then flip discretely — that's why we compute sensitivity, not just solutions
75 more oven minutes → new plan (42, 49) worth $5,040: the shadow price idea, coming in Session 3

agenda.title: The Same Model in Gurobi + Wrap-Up
agenda.description: The bakery model in gurobipy on Colab: eleven lines of Python reproduce the graphical answer instantly — and scale to problems with a million variables where pictures can't go.
bulletPoints: model.addVar, setObjective, addConstr, optimize — the pattern you'll use all semester
Homework: re-run tonight's what-ifs in code, claim your free Gurobi academic license

activities.title: The Bakery Model in gurobipy
activities.description: A bakery produces bread and cakes in batches. Bread contributes $50/batch, cake $60/batch. Weekly demand caps: 90 batches of bread, 60 of cake. A batch of bread needs 60 minutes of oven time and 30 of labor; cake needs 45 and 60. Available: 4,650 oven minutes, 4,200 labor minutes.

steps.title: Formulate on paper first
steps.description: Two decision variables (batches of bread B, batches of cake C), one objective (maximize 50B + 60C), four constraints (two demand caps, oven time, labor time).

steps.title: Solve it graphically
steps.description: Draw each constraint line, shade the feasible set, and slide the $-profit line outward. It last touches the region at the corner (40, 50) — profit $5,000.

steps.title: Confirm with the solver
steps.description: Run the gurobipy cell and check that the industrial solver lands on exactly the corner your picture predicted.

steps.title: Stress-test the decision
steps.description: Re-solve with bread profit at $40, $30, and $20, then with 75 extra oven minutes. Watch when the plan holds, when it jumps corners, and what an extra resource is worth.

codeBlock.code:
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

model = gp.Model('bakery_production')

bread = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name='bread', lb=0, ub=90)
cake = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name='cake', lb=0, ub=60)

model.setObjective(50*bread + 60*cake, GRB.MAXIMIZE)
model.addConstr(60*bread + 45*cake <= 4650, 'oven_time')
model.addConstr(30*bread + 60*cake <= 4200, 'labor_time')

model.optimize()
print(f'bread: {bread.X:.0f} batches, cake: {cake.X:.0f} batches')
print(f'Maximum profit: ${model.ObjVal:,.0f}')

activities.discussionNote: Notice what the solver gives you that the picture cannot: it scales. The graphical method dies at two variables — gurobipy solves the same grammar with two million variables. And it returns a certificate of optimality: not a good answer, the provably best one.

takeaways.text: Prescriptive analytics is the top of the value chain: descriptive → predictive → prescriptive. Prediction is an input; the decision is the product.
Every optimization model has exactly three ingredients — decision variables, an objective, and constraints — and the optimum of a linear program always sits at a corner of the feasible set.
Optimal decisions are stable within ranges, then jump: bread at $40 keeps the plan, bread at $20 flips it to another corner. Knowing where those cliffs are is sensitivity analysis — Session 3.
